title: Erdős #1: Structural Theory of Distinct Subset Sums
description: Structural foundations for Erdős Problem #1 (Distinct Subset Sums). Proves the superincreasing extension lemma (the key construction principle), establishes that powers of 2 always yield DSS sets, proves DSS existence for any n (filling the gap in OQ03's minDSSBound), and derives elementary structural constraints: all elements must be positive, and the total sum satisfies sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. All results are fully proved in Lean 4.
originalContributions: dss_superincreasing_extend: If A has DSS and b > sum(A), then insert b A has DSS (the key structural lemma)
powers_of_two_has_dss: {1,2,4,...,2^(n-1)} has distinct subset sums for any n (inductive proof via superincreasing)
dss_exists: For any n, there exists an n-element set with DSS (existential witness for minDSSBound)
not_dss_of_mem_zero: If 0 ∈ A, then A does NOT have DSS (∅ and {0} give same sum)
dss_elements_pos: All elements of a DSS nonempty set are positive
dss_subset: Any subset of a DSS set also has DSS (monotone property)
dss_sum_lower_bound: sum(A) + 1 ≥ 2^n for any n-element DSS set A
minDSS_witness: Fills the sorry in OQ03's minDSSBound definition

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #1 (1931, $500 prize) asks whether any set of n positive integers with all 2^n subset sums distinct (a DSS set) must have maximum element ≥ c · 2^n for some absolute constant c > 0. The problem remained open for decades; the best known upper bound c ≤ 0.22009 comes from the Conway-Guy sequence (1968). The counting lower bound max(A) ≥ 2^(n-1)/n was proved by Erdős and Moser; the DFX information-theoretic bound (Dubroff-Fox-Xu, 2021) improves the constant by a log factor.

The superincreasing extension lemma at the heart of this file is classical: it is the reason the powers-of-2 set {1, 2, 4, ..., 2^(n-1)} has DSS (proved by induction). All greedy DSS constructions follow this pattern. The gallery formalizes the counting bound (OQ01), DFX entropy framework (OQ02), Conway-Guy sequence (OQ03), and extremal sets (OQ04). This WIP file adds the structural foundations that underlie all those results.
overview.problemStatement:
If A ⊆ ℕ has the distinct subset sums property (∀ S T ⊆ A, sum(S) = sum(T) → S = T), what structural constraints must A satisfy? In particular:
1. When can we extend A while preserving DSS?
2. What is the canonical construction giving DSS sets of any size?
3. What are the necessary conditions on elements?
overview.proofStrategy:
The central tool is the **superincreasing extension lemma**: if A has DSS and b > sum(A), then A ∪ {b} has DSS. The proof is by case analysis on whether b is in each of the two subsets:
- Both contain b: subtract b from both sums, apply DSS of A.
- b in one but not the other: the sum with b is > sum(A), while the sum without is ≤ sum(A). Contradiction.
- Neither contains b: both subsets lie in A; apply DSS of A directly.

From this lemma, powers of 2 give DSS (by induction: 2^n > ∑_{i<n} 2^i), and existence for any n follows immediately.
keyInsights: The superincreasing extension lemma is the constructive core of all known DSS constructions. Both the Conway-Guy sequence and the powers-of-2 sequence are superincreasing, which is why they have DSS.
0 cannot be in a DSS set: ∅ and {0} would both have sum 0 but be distinct subsets. This forces all elements positive.
The sum lower bound sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1 (for n-element DSS A) is derived from the injective pigeonhole argument: 2^n subset sums in [0, sum(A)] forces 2^n ≤ sum(A) + 1.
The DSS monotone property (any subset of a DSS set has DSS) means the problem has a hereditary structure — the DSS 'language' is an antichain under inclusion.

The dss_exists theorem fills the sorry in OQ03's minDSSBound definition, which uses Nat.find to find the minimum element bound. Lean's Nat.find requires a proof of existence as input; dss_positive_exists provides exactly this witness, making the entire OQ03 construction well-founded.

sections.title: Imports and Header
sections.summary: File header describing the seven structural results, references to Erdős (1955), Dubroff-Fox-Xu (2021), Conway-Guy (1968), and OEIS A005318. Imports Proofs.Erdos1Problem (the hasDistinctSubsetSums predicate) and opens Finset namespace.

sections.title: Part I: Superincreasing Extension Lemma
sections.summary: dss_superincreasing_extend: if A has DSS and b > sum(A) with b ∉ A, then insert b A has DSS. Proved by four-way case split on b ∈ S, b ∈ T. The combinatorial core underlying all known DSS constructions.

sections.title: Part II: Geometric Sum Bound
sections.summary: sum_two_pow_range_add_one (private): ∑_{i<n} 2^i + 1 = 2^n by induction. sum_two_pow_lt: ∑_{i<n} 2^i < 2^n by linarith. Provides the superincreasing property for powers of 2.
sections.mathContext: $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} 2^i = 2^n - 1$, proved by induction, providing the strict bound $2^n > \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} 2^i$ needed for the superincreasing extension step.

sections.title: Part III: Powers of 2 Give DSS
sections.summary: powers_of_two_has_dss: {2^0, 2^1, …, 2^(n-1)} has distinct subset sums for any n. Proved by induction via dss_superincreasing_extend. Uses Finset.sum_image with injectivity of i ↦ 2^i.
sections.mathContext: The set $\{1, 2, 4, \ldots, 2^{n-1}\}$ represents the $n$-bit binary numbers: its $2^n$ subsets have sums $0, 1, \ldots, 2^n - 1$, all distinct.

sections.title: Part IV: DSS Existence for Any n
sections.summary: dss_exists: ∃ A with |A| = n, all elements ≤ n·2^n, and DSS. dss_positive_exists: ∃ A with |A| = n, all elements positive and ≤ 2^n, and DSS. Both use the powers-of-2 witness. Fills the sorry in OQ03's minDSSBound.

sections.title: Part V: Structural Properties
sections.summary: not_dss_of_mem_zero: 0 ∈ A destroys DSS (∅ and {0} have same sum). dss_elements_pos: all elements of a DSS set are positive. dss_subset: hereditary property — any subset of a DSS set has DSS. dss_singleton: any singleton has DSS.

sections.title: Part VI: Sum Lower Bound
sections.summary: dss_sum_lower_bound: 2^n ≤ sum(A) + 1 for any n-element DSS set A (by pigeonhole on the 2^n distinct subset sums in [0, sum(A)]). dss_sum_ge_pow_sub_one: sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1 as corollary.
sections.mathContext: The $2^n$ distinct subset sums lie in $\{0, \ldots, \sum(A)\}$, forcing $2^n \leq \sum(A) + 1$ by injectivity counting. This global bound implies $\max(A) \geq (2^n-1)/n$.

sections.title: Part VII: Connection to OQ03 minDSSBound
sections.summary: minDSS_witness: ∃ N, ∃ A, |A| = n ∧ (∀ a ∈ A, a ≤ N) ∧ DSS(A). One-liner delegating to dss_exists. Fills the sorry that blocked OQ03's Nat.find-based minDSSBound definition.

crossReferences.description: The main Erdős Problem #1 gallery entry — this WIP file provides structural foundations that support the OQ01–OQ04 sub-entries
OQ01 proves the counting lower bound max(A) ≥ 2^(n-1)/n via pigeonhole — the same argument that this file generalizes to the global sum lower bound sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1
OQ02's DFX entropy framework (Dubroff-Fox-Xu 2021) uses information-theoretic methods to improve the constant in the lower bound — complementing this file's elementary pigeonhole approach
OQ03 defines minDSSBound using Nat.find, which requires the existential witness now provided by dss_exists / minDSS_witness in this file — directly filling OQ03's sorry
OQ04 studies extremal DSS sets (those achieving the minimum max element) — the structural constraints proved here (positivity, sum lower bound) are necessary conditions for extremality

conclusion.summary: This file provides the structural foundations for Erdős Problem #1: the superincreasing extension lemma (the construction principle behind all known DSS sets), the powers-of-2 DSS construction (proved by induction), existence of DSS sets for any n (filling the sorry in OQ03), positivity of elements, and the global sum lower bound. All results have 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The superincreasing lemma gives a recursive DSS construction: start with A = {} and repeatedly add any element larger than the current sum. This shows DSS sets are not 'rare' — they can be built greedily. The powers-of-2 construction is the smallest such greedy sequence. The Conway-Guy sequence (OQ03) is a more efficient greedy strategy that nearly achieves the conjectured optimal constant c = 1/(2π^{1/2}) ≈ 0.28.
openQuestions: Erdős $500 conjecture: must max(A) ≥ c · 2^n for some absolute c > 0?
What is the exact constant c? Upper bound c ≤ 0.22009 (Conway-Guy 1968).
Is the Conway-Guy sequence optimal? (Open for n > 10)
